pages.text: Overnight rain swelled the river, muddy yellow. Grandpa's boat floated tied to a post. Bung chewed fruit from a basket.
Bung wanted a red fruit for Ddori too. But the basket was empty. That had been the last. "No more, Ddori. What now?"
A red fruit floated downriver. "One there!" A wave pushed it aboard. Bung picked it up and lifted it toward the mouth.
"Ah! Ah!" Ddori pushed Bung's arm away. Grandpa caught the hand too. "Where did that fruit come from?"
Grandpa laid basket fruit and floating fruit together on the floor. A finger pressed the basket fruit: firm. In the floating fruit, it sank right in.
"Long floating makes the inside soft. Eating it gives you a tummy ache." Bung put it down. "Do not eat floating fruit!"
Soon a green fruit floated past. Bung hid both hands behind the back. "Do not eat floating fruit!" Then Bung called Grandpa.
He pushed it away with a long piece of wood. "Thank you for asking." The boat rocked. Sitting down, Bung drew Ddori's hand close.
A wood piece floated by. Bung held both hands behind the back. "One, do not scoop floating things out! Two, keep them from your mouth! Three, show Grandpa! Do not eat floating fruit!"
Water dropped, sun sinking. Grandpa stroked Bung's back. "Not eating unknown things keeps you strongest." Bung gave Ddori fresh fruit. "Do not eat floating fruit!"
